MOLECULAR GENETICS LABORATORY REPORT

Patient: [redacted name]
DOB: [redacted date]
MRN: [redacted ID]
Specimen ID: [redacted ID]
Specimen Type: Peripheral blood
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

REFERRAL REASON
Targeted mutation analysis for common BRCA1 and BRCA2 mutations associated with Ashkenazi Jewish/Polish ancestry.

METHODOLOGY
DNA was extracted from peripheral blood and analyzed by targeted sequencing for the following specific mutations:

BRCA1 (LRG_292t1):
• c.68_69delAG (185delAG)
• c.181T>G (300T>G)
• c.3700_3704del5 (3819del5)
• c.4034delA (4153delA)
• c.5266dupC (5382insC)

BRCA2 (LRG_293t1):
• c.5946delT (6174delT)

Sequencing was performed using next-generation sequencing technology with minimum coverage of 100x for all targeted regions.

RESULTS
No mutations detected in the analyzed regions.

BRCA1: c.68_69delAG - Not detected
BRCA1: c.181T>G - Not detected
BRCA1: c.3700_3704del5 - Not detected
BRCA1: c.4034delA - Not detected
BRCA1: c.5266dupC - Not detected
BRCA2: c.5946delT - Not detected

TECHNICAL NOTES
Nomenclature follows HGVS guidelines. Reference sequences used: LRG_292t1 (BRCA1) and LRG_293t1 (BRCA2). Nucleotide numbering begins from the first base of the translation initiation codon (ATG).

This targeted panel tests for specific founder mutations common in individuals of Ashkenazi Jewish and Polish ancestry. These mutations account for approximately 90% of BRCA1/BRCA2 mutations in the Ashkenazi Jewish population.

The absence of these common mutations reduces the likelihood of hereditary breast and ovarian cancer syndrome through these specific pathways. However, this test does not exclude the possibility of other pathogenic variants in BRCA1, BRCA2, or other cancer predisposition genes.

Reported by: [redacted name], PhD
Laboratory Director: [redacted name], MD, PhD
